title: Randomness, Gap Rules, Trig Type, Carets & Hints
description: CSS random() with a seeded resolver, gap decorations, trigonometric type, a shapeable caret, and a tooltip stack that stops closing menus.

drops.title: Seeded Random
drops.description: Scatter, jitter and tilt authored as real random() syntax in CSS, resolved by a seeded reader so the same seed rebuilds the same scene.
drops.concept: CSS is gaining a random() function, and the trick that makes it usable today is that custom properties accept almost any token sequence — so `--random-size: random(1px, 5px, 1px)` survives parsing and can be read straight back out of the computed style. This drop collects every --random* declaration the page makes, resolves it with a deterministic PRNG, and writes the answer back, including the element-shared keyword that gives a whole set one shared value.
drops.source: CSS-Tricks — 'Let's Use the Emergent CSS random() Function in all the Browsers'

interaction.mouse: Drag the seed and spread sliders to re-roll the starfield, confetti and hand-set headline
interaction.click: Roll new seed picks a fresh reproducible scene
interaction.touch: The tuner drops inline under the header on narrow screens

drops.title: Gap Rules
drops.description: Grid and flex now take column-rule, and row-rule paints the horizontal gaps — dividers that live inside the gap and never shift the layout.
drops.concept: Dividers used to mean a border on every child or a pseudo-element hack. Gap decorations move the job to the container, so the lines sit in the gap itself, disappear when a row wraps, and break cleanly around items that span tracks. Where the browser has not shipped them yet, this page paints the same rules from script — including the segmentation around spanning cells — so the knobs behave identically either way.
drops.source: utilitybend (Brecht De Ruyte) — 'CSS is filling the gaps with rules'

interaction.mouse: Sliders drive rule width, gap size and inset; segments pick the line style
interaction.click: Colour swatches recolour every rule at once
interaction.touch: Resize or rotate the device to watch the wrap gap clear itself

drops.title: Trig Type
drops.description: Rings, arcs, spirals and a travelling sine wave — every glyph placed by cos() and sin() inside a single calc().
drops.concept: CSS trigonometry turns a flat row of glyphs into polar layout without any layout maths in JavaScript. Script does one job: split the word and hand each letter its index. The stylesheet turns that index into an angle, then into a position with translate(r*cos(a), r*sin(a)) and a tangential rotation. The wave scene animates an @property-registered angle so the phase travels through sin() on the compositor.
drops.source: Carmen Ansio — 'CSS Trigonometry: Circular Layouts with sin() and cos()'

interaction.mouse: Radius, sweep and start-angle sliders reshape the ring and the arc headline live
interaction.click: Toggle tangent rotation to see the difference between placed and oriented glyphs
interaction.touch: Controls stack above the scenes on narrow screens

drops.title: Caret Craft
drops.description: The last unstylable part of a text field gives in: caret-shape makes the cursor a block, a bar or an underscore.
drops.concept: caret-shape finally lets the text cursor be a design decision — bar for a seam, block for a place, underscore for a terminal — and the caret shorthand sets shape and colour together. Because the property is new, this drop also draws a stand-in caret by measuring the text before the insertion point, so you can compare all three shapes on any browser and switch renderers by hand.
drops.source: Manuel Rego, Igalia — 'Playing with the new caret CSS properties'

interaction.mouse: Click into any of the four fields and type; the shape, colour and blink knobs apply live
interaction.click: Cycle the renderer between native and the measured stand-in
interaction.touch: Tap a field to focus it, then switch shapes from the inline panel

drops.title: Hint Popovers
drops.description: popover="hint" gives tooltips a top-layer stack of their own, so hovering a menu row stops slamming the menu shut.
drops.concept: Every tooltip library eventually hits the same wall: open a menu, hover an item, and the tooltip dismisses the menu because both compete for one stack. The hint state fixes it — a hint never dismisses an auto popover, and a nested hint does not dismiss the hint that contains it. The two lanes here run identical markup, one with hints and one with autos, so you can watch the failure and the fix side by side with a live top-layer readout.

interaction.mouse: Open either Layers menu and hover the rows; hover the ? inside a tooltip for a nested hint
interaction.click: The toolbar buttons open and close the auto popovers
interaction.touch: Tap a toolbar button to open a menu; tapping a row shows its tooltip
